https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-raymond-james-joins-the-iphone-cut-parade-1516918674 Apple: Which iPhones Go, Which Stay in 2018? By Jan. 25, 2018 5:17 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
If it’s a Thursday, which it is, it must be time for another cut to the forecast for Apple ’s ( AAPL ) iPhone production. 
Earlier today, Chris Caso , semiconductor analyst with Raymond James , reported that suppliers to Apple with whom he spoke just two weeks ago, at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, “now have lower expectations” for iPhone. 
The “proximate cause,” he writes, is an “ unusual product transition ,” whereby Apple is discontinuing the existing iPhone X later this year, to replace it with two new models, which he’s referring to as “ iPhone Xs ," something that had been rumored earlier this week in a report from KGI Securities . 
As a result, he sees sales of iPhone in the March quarter of perhaps 55 million, which is consistent with what Bernstein 's Toni Sacconaghi wrote yesterday when he opined Apple's March-quarter outlook may disappoint. (Apple is set to report next Thursday, February 1st.) 
Why wold Apple do that? he asks. Perhaps because the new model will have things such as “support for 4x4 MIMO,” a wireless networking capability that boosts bandwidth, along with larger screens on the two new models and a new Apple chip, of course. 
All that means, perhaps, that it "may not have left room for both iPhone X and iPhone Xs to remain in the lineup together." 
But Caso writes that it’s not clear entirely how much of this is the production choice for Apple, and how much reflects weaker demand : 
While we think this production change is mainly the result of that inventory adjustment, we simply don’t know how much might also be demand related. We did not detect incremental changes in iPhone 8 production (yet we believe iPhone 8 production had already experienced cuts in December). Therefore, these incremental changes only affect about 30% of the total iPhone mix, but because the changes are significant and iPhone X has more content than other iPhones, we nonetheless believe the effect is material. 
A further mystery is what happens to the just-released iPhone 8 , as well as last year's iPhone 7 , especially given "the 7 [is] seemingly holding in better than expected," according to Caso's contacts. 
Will Apple keep them in the lineup? He notes "it seems unlikely" if, as rumored, Apple's also bringing out a "new higher-end LCD model," but then he adds, "none of our contacts has insight into which one stays and what the resulting impact on inventories would be. Net, this could be another shoe to drop." 
The upshot of all that is an “air pocket” for some suppliers, and he cuts estimates on Qorvo ( QRVO ) and Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ): 
Importantly, while we could see an air pocket for production of some components in the near term, particularly in 2Q, this effect is transitory–we would expect to see production begin to ramp up in the June and September quarters. Net,whatever flagship inventory is burned through in the first-half of 2018 will need to be put back in place in the back-half of the year. In addition, if suppliers are supplying components that are identical between iPhone X and iPhone Xs, such suppliers are likely to experience a more muted effect from this transition. We don’t expect the RF suppliers to fall into that camp, since we expect the RF subsystem to be re-architected for iPhone Xs and Xs Plus. 
Those words of caution and encouragement echo a note on Tuesday from Macquarie 's Srini Pajjuri about Qorvo and Skyworks. 
Apple shares today declined by $3.11, or 1.8%, to close at $171.11. Qorvo stock fell by 84 cents, or 1.3%, to $66.06. Skyworks closed down by $2.08, or 2%, at $95.05. Broadcom ( AVGO ), another Apple wireless supplier, closed down by $9.57, or almost 4%, at $247.29. Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and Intel ( INTC ), which compete to sell " baseband " chips into the iPhone, declined fractionally. And Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ), the sometime fabrication partner for Apple's chips, declined by half a percent. Most Popular
